Quiet about you, too.

Window positions, never pixels.

Hush asks macOS which window is in front and where it sits. It never asks for Screen Recording and never sees what’s inside a window.

No account. No analytics.

There is nothing to sign up for and nothing counting what you do. Your settings stay in your Mac’s preferences.

One small check a day.

The only time Hush goes online is to ask GitHub whether there’s a new version. Turn that off in Settings whenever you like.

Good to know

Hush needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later and runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. It dims every connected display.
To know which window is in front. Accessibility tells Hush when focus changes, so it can tuck the shade right behind that window. It doesn’t read your screen.
Unzip the download, move Hush to Applications and open it. Then allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility. Hush is in early preview and not yet notarized by Apple, so the first time, macOS asks you to choose Open Anyway in the same Privacy & Security pane.
Menus, alerts and system panels stay above the shade. Apps on your exceptions list switch dimming off while they’re in front. If Hush can’t match a window, it leaves the screen undimmed rather than guess.
Hush checks GitHub once a day and offers new versions in a small window. You can check by hand from the menu bar or turn automatic checks off in Settings.
Yes. No price, no trial, no account. The source code is on GitHub.

Hush needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later and runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. It dims every connected display.
